analysis:
Examined the benchmark runner change (SchedulerPrefillDecisionLiveRunner.swift:66-81, 101-102), the new prefill-geometry resolution in EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift (lines 58-161, 172-183, 395-404), and the build-metadata plumbing in EngineV2Factory+Production.swift. The changes are scheduler tuning: a Gemma 4 default plain chunk of 2048, a step-token budget, a new env-overridable prefill chunk and step-budget pair, and exposure of the resolved geometry on ProductionBuild.

No trust-boundary change was found. The coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), attestation (TB-009/TB-011), keys and authorization are untouched. The new env keys DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS are read from the provider process environment, which is operator-controlled. Operator control of the process is already in the TB-003 threat model, so they add no new consumer-reachable surface.

Consumer-reachable concerns: Gemma 4 media-block handling raises the chunk to 1120 and the step budget to at least 1120 when overrides are small (lines 97-106). This keeps submit validation consistent and does not appear to widen consumer capability. The Nemotron calibrated bound (lines 186-193) still clamps the chunk after geometry resolution, so overrides cannot widen it. One possible gap is that the step budget is not clamped to the calibrated limit, but I did not verify whether the scheduler enforces that elsewhere. The doubled-budget default uses overflow-safe arithmetic. An explicit huge step budget is accepted. A larger step budget or chunk raises transient activation memory, an availability and DoS consideration under T-010/T-029, but Gemma 4 behavior is documented as measured. Other families are unchanged unless the operator sets overrides.

Prefix cache (T-041): the cache salt, SSD tier, TTL and HMAC naming are untouched. Chunk size changes could alter block-boundary and TTFT characteristics, but SEC-035 is already an accepted risk and no new leak is evident.

Open questions for integration: whether the CBv2 scheduler and paged-KV preconditions (PagedSequenceKV ring sizing, CBv2MultimodalPlan.validate) hold with the new chunk and stripe combinations. Those sources were not supplied, so I could not verify them.
